head_q: How have advancements in diffusion and autoregressive models improved the quality of AI-generated images?
tail_q: What role does a semantic-level textual branch play in multi-modal feature fusion and detection?
head: arXiv:2608.07863v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Driven by advances in diffusion models and autoregressive models, the fidelity and resolution of AI-generated images now rival those of real images.

head_q: How do agents make decisions regarding model selection, tool usage, and input relevance in task execution?
tail_q: What errors and confounds affect the accuracy of headline deployment claims in analysis?
head: arXiv:2610.02267v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agent harnesses make many small, typed decisions per task: which model to call, which tool to use, whether retrieved text is relevant, whether an input carries an injection.
tail: Three analysis errors and one design confound distorted headline deployment claims: an omitted pre-screen cost (reported 23.9% saving, actual 4.3%), gate accuracy reported as end-to-end quality (58% vs. 98%), in-sample thresholds (5% target, up to 17% held-out misses), and a "channel effect" on injection false positives that vanishes with channel-native content.

head_q: What is the iTeach system and how does it allow humans to correct a robot's perception errors?
tail_q: How does downstream pick-and-place performance on SceneReplica compare to model-based pipelines using CAD models?
head: arXiv:2410.09072v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present iTeach, a deployable system that lets any co-located human fix a robot's perception failures on the spot without expertise, a workstation, or offline retraining.
tail: Downstream pick-and-place on SceneReplica reaches 72/100, surpassing a model-based pipeline requiring CAD models.

head_q: What are the limitations of neural surrogate models for PDEs on unstructured 3D geometries?
tail_q: How does this methodology enable data-efficient neural emulators for large-scale simulations?
head: arXiv:2610.03363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural surrogate models for Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) on unstructured 3D geometries are often limited by poor generalization and the high cost of generating large-scale training datasets.
tail: This methodology provides a practical pathway toward data-efficient neural emulators for large-scale simulations.

head_q: What advancements have Multimodal Large Language Models made in visual-language tasks and artistic evaluation?
tail_q: How does educator-aligned supervision improve evaluations in educational AI systems?
head: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) show remarkable progress across many visual-language tasks; however, their capacity to evaluate artistic expression remains limited.
tail: These results show that educator-aligned supervision and attribute-aware training yield pedagogically meaningful evaluations and establish a rigorous testbed for sustained progress in educational AI.

head_q: What challenges do 3D CNNs face in automated analysis of volumetric medical imaging on edge devices?
tail_q: How does this method provide a scalable solution for real-time patient prioritization in resource-limited settings?
head: Automated analysis of volumetric medical imaging on edge devices is severely constrained by the high memory and computational demands of 3D Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs).
tail: By approximating 3D contextual reasoning at a fraction of the computational cost, this method provides a scalable solution for real-time patient prioritization in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile stroke units and IoT-enabled remote clinics.

head_q: What potential do AI models have in imaging for acute ischemic stroke, particularly in lesion detection?
tail_q: How does the framework integrate visual explanations to enhance decision-making in medical imaging?
head: Artificial intelligence models have shown strong potential in acute ischemic stroke imaging, particularly for lesion detection and segmentation using computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging.
tail: The framework further integrates visual explanation mechanisms to support both predictive and abstention decisions, addressing a key limitation of existing uncertainty aware medical imaging systems.

head_q: What issues do quantum neural networks face due to gate-level redundancy in NISQ devices?
tail_q: What is the computational feasibility of the pruning procedure in quantum neural networks?
head: Quantum neural networks (QNNs) suffer from severe gate-level redundancy, which hinders their deployment on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices.
tail: Third, we prove that the pruning procedure is computationally feasible, requiring only polynomial-time comparisons and avoiding exponential enumeration over the Hilbert space.

head_q: How are item-to-item relationships utilized to improve recommendation systems beyond user-item modeling?
tail_q: What evidence supports the effectiveness and efficiency of our method compared to state-of-the-art diversity models?
head: Beyond user-item modeling, item-to-item relationships are increasingly used to enhance recommendation.
tail: Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art diversity models in both diversity and accuracy, and further validates its effectiveness, transferability, and efficiency over baselines.

head_q: What challenges does photorealistic 3-D reconstruction face in large scenes when depth, pose, and radiance are addressed separately?
tail_q: Can high-quality 3-D reconstruction and novel-view synthesis be achieved using a single uncalibrated RGB camera?
head: Photorealistic 3-D reconstruction from monocular video collapses in large-scale scenes when depth, pose, and radiance are solved in isolation: scale-ambiguous depth yields ghost geometry, long-horizon pose drift corrupts alignment, and a single global NeRF cannot model hundreds of metres of content.
tail: These results demonstrate that metric-scale, drift-free 3-D reconstruction and high-fidelity novel-view synthesis are achievable from a single uncalibrated RGB camera.

head_q: What research exists on dialect-specific Automatic Speech Recognition systems for low-resource Arabic dialects like Sudanese?
tail_q: How are models, benchmarks, and training pipelines for low-resource Arabic ASR made publicly available?
head: Although many Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems have been developed for Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) and Dialectal Arabic (DA), few studies have focused on dialect-specific implementations, particularly for low-resource Arabic dialects such as Sudanese.
tail: The models, evaluation benchmarks, and reproducible training pipelines are publicly released to facilitate future research on low-resource Arabic ASR.

head_q: How do GPU kernels generated by large language models compare to expert implementations in terms of efficiency?
tail_q: What is the average combined implementation score across various models in a specific study?
head: arXiv:2610.03226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GPU kernels generated by large language model (LLM) agents can remain less efficient than expert implementations, but runtime alone does not reveal how the gap relates to design discovery and implementation.
tail: Across all five models, the mean combined implementation score increases from 57 to 70 out of 100.

head_q: How is artificial intelligence impacting public sector processes in Gulf Cooperation Council countries, considering their unique characteristics?
tail_q: What guidance does the index provide for policymakers regarding ethical and regulatory standards in AI deployment?
head: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming public-sector processes worldwide, yet standardized measures rarely address the unique drivers, governance models, and cultural nuances of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries.
tail: The index offers actionable guidance for policymakers seeking to harmonize large-scale deployments with ethical and regulatory standards.

tail_q: How are structured references and instructions integrated into prompts for video generation?
head: arXiv:2609.37407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While recent video foundation models excel at generating high-quality short videos, long-form video generation remains a critical challenge, where a major bottleneck lies in conditioning independently generated shots to preserve consistent characters, scenes, and objects throughout a story.
tail: Finally, the retrieved references, structured element states, and grounding instructions are assembled into a unified prompt for the frozen video generator.

head_q: How does the ability to manipulate tools enhance a robot's task performance?

head: arXiv:2602.16863v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The ability to manipulate tools significantly expands the set of tasks a robot can perform.

head_q: How does exposure to violent content in music affect listeners' emotions and behaviors?
tail_q: What potential does Generative AI have in creating safer listening experiences while maintaining artistic integrity?
head: Repeated exposure to violence and abusive content in music and song content can influence listeners' emotions and behaviours, potentially normalising aggression or reinforcing harmful stereotypes.

head: arXiv:2610.08420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a polynomial sample complexity separation between symmetry-aware and symmetry-agnostic feature learning.

head: Foundation models (FMs) are driving a prominent shift in artificial intelligence across different domains, including biomedical imaging.
tail: We conclude that while the vision of autonomous AI-doctors remains distant, the immediate reality is the emergence of powerful technology and assistive tools that would benefit clinical practice.

head: arXiv:2610.07829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic sensing (SemS) acquires task-relevant information rather than reconstructing complete physical information.

head_q: How does quantum chemistry support various scientific fields such as materials science and computational biology?
tail_q: What are the current challenges and future directions for fully autonomous computational chemistry research agents?
head: Quantum chemistry is a foundational enabling tool for the fields of chemistry, materials science, computational biology and others.

head: Machine unlearning aims to remove the influence of specific data points from a trained model to satisfy privacy, copyright, and safety requirements.

tail_q: How does minimizing Kullback-Leibler divergence affect the risk of merged models?
head: Model merging has emerged as a lightweight alternative to joint multi-task learning (MTL), yet the generalization properties of merged models remain largely unexplored.

tail_q: How does the Gini coefficient behave when analyzing only buggy code variants?
head: Large language models are increasingly used for code generation and debugging, but their outputs can still contain bugs, that originate from training data.

head: arXiv:2610.13071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vulnerability patching is critical for safeguarding an enterprise's software ecosystem from cyber attacks.

head: Recent studies suggest that Visual Language Models (VLMs) hold great potential for tasks such as automated medical diagnosis.

head_q: How has reinforcement learning been utilized to fine-tune generative models to meet human preferences?
tail_q: What improvements in task alignment and generation diversity does DRIFT achieve compared to other methods?
head: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for fine-tuning large-scale generative models, such as diffusion and flow models, to align with complex human preferences and user-specified tasks.
tail: Experimental results show that DRIFT achieves superior Pareto dominance regarding task alignment and generation diversity, yielding a $ 9.08\%\!\sim\! 43.46\%$ increase in diversity at equivalent alignment levels and a $ 59.65\% \!\sim\! 65.86\%$ increase in alignment at equivalent levels of diversity.

head_q: How do Security Information and Event Management systems function in monitoring IT infrastructure for large organizations?
tail_q: How does SynRAG perform against leading language models in the context of SIEM systems?
head: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems are essential for large enterprises to monitor their IT infrastructure by ingesting and analyzing millions of logs and events daily.
tail: We evaluate SynRAG against state-of-the-art language models, including GPT, Llama, DeepSeek, Gemma, and Claude, using Qradar and SecOps as representative SIEM systems.

head_q: How has the development of large language models transformed AI agents into decision-making entities?
tail_q: What intrinsic tasks can Sophia perform independently, and how does it reduce reasoning steps?
head: The development of LLMs has elevated AI agents from task-specific tools to long-lived, decision-making entities.
tail: Quantitatively, Sophia independently initiates and executes various intrinsic tasks while achieving an 80% reduction in reasoning steps for recurring operations.

head_q: How do large language models achieve expert-level performance in competitive mathematics through search volume?
tail_q: What factors contribute to the observed asymmetry in model capabilities across different tested models?
head: arXiv:2610.03551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have reached expert-level performance on competition mathematics largely through the volume of search placed around them: candidate solutions are sampled in quantity and retained only when an external criterion accepts them.
tail: Capability does not govern the asymmetry: it appears in every model tested, and the most capable widens least.

head_q: What scalable methods exist for identifying patients at risk of opioid overdose?

head: arXiv:2609.40108v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Opioid overdose remains a major clinical and public health burden, highlighting the need for scalable approaches to identify patients at high risk.

head_q: What are the privacy concerns associated with Audio Large Language Models?

head: While Audio Large Language Models (ALLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in understanding and generation, their potential privacy implications remain largely unexplored.
tail: These findings expose critical vulnerabilities in ALLMs, underscoring the urgent need for targeted privacy alignment.

head: arXiv:2510.12132v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Remote physiological measurement gained wide attention, while it requires collecting users' privacy-sensitive information, and existing contactless measurements still rely on labeled client data.

head_q: What limitations do current text-to-image generation models have with user prompts?

head: arXiv:2510.12041v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent advances in text-to-image (T2I) generation have achieved impressive results, yet existing models often struggle with simple or underspecified user prompts due to a distributional gap with their descriptive training captions.
tail: Furthermore, we demonstrate strong transferability by showing that a rewriter trained on one T2I backbone generalizes effectively to others without needing to be retrained.

head_q: What role do normalized difference indices play in remote sensing applications?

head: Normalized difference indices have been a staple in remote sensing for decades.

head_q: What is the impact of overparameterization on generalization in deep learning models?
tail_q: How does overfitting affect model performance in relation to empirical and true scores?
head: arXiv:2609.26392v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Conventional wisdom in deep learning holds that overparameterization---having more parameters $p$ than training samples $n$---is benign: larger models generalize better and, even without regularization, interpolating models generalize well, the test error following a double-descent curve.
tail: This overfitting is malign because, although the implicit regularization of training is fully at work, it drives the model toward the empirical score, which memorizes the training set, rather than toward the true score.

head_q: What improvements can be made to linear programming accuracy using diagonal matrices?
tail_q: How can the efficiency of solving linear systems in linear programming be enhanced?
head: arXiv:2609.30853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lee and Sidford [LS19] showed that the linear program $\min\{c^\top x\ :\ A^\top x=b,\ l\leq x\leq u\}$ over $x\in\mathbb{R}^m$, where $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, can be solved to accuracy $\epsilon$ using $O(\sqrt n\log^{13}m\cdot\log(mU/\epsilon))$ solves of linear systems in $A^\top\mathbf DA$ for positive diagonal matrices $\mathbf D$, where $U$ bounds the magnitudes of the input and of the initial point.
tail: Given an interior point and a finite certified magnitude bound $U$, we give an algorithm that uses $O(\sqrt n\log^{4}m\cdot\log(mU/\epsilon))$ solves of such linear systems, improving the Lee--Sidford bound by a factor of $\log^{9}m$.

head_q: What novel optimization methods are available for predicting optimal transport plans?
tail_q: What applications have been tested for the proposed optimal transport methods?
head: arXiv:2604.15114v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a novel amortized optimization method for predicting optimal transport (OT) plans across multiple pairs of measures by leveraging Kantorovich potentials derived from sliced OT.
tail: We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approaches on tasks including MNIST digit transport, color transfer, supply-demand transportation on spherical data, and mini-batch OT conditional flow matching.

head_q: How is artificial intelligence expected to change the field of medical imaging?
tail_q: What advantages does MHub.ai offer for benchmarking clinical models?

head_q: How does machine learning facilitate vulnerabilities in finance and healthcare systems?
tail_q: What are the main types of attacks targeting foundation models in critical infrastructure?
head: Machine learning (ML) underpins foundation models in finance, healthcare, and critical infrastructure, making them targets for data poisoning, model extraction, prompt injection, automated jailbreaking, and preference-guided black-box attacks that exploit model comparisons.
tail: Dominant TTPs include MASTERKEY-style jailbreaking, federated poisoning, diffusion backdoors, and preference optimization leakage, mainly impacting pre-training and inference.

head_q: How is unstructured data like images and text utilized in empirical economic research?

head_q: What processes do global gridded crop models use to simulate crop growth and yield projections?

head: Global gridded crop models (GGCMs) simulate daily crop growth by explicitly representing key biophysical processes and project end-of-season yield time series.

head_q: What limitations do multimodal large language models face regarding input and output processing?
tail_q: Where can I access the code for the Speak-While-Watching project?
head: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved strong performance across many tasks, yet most systems remain limited to offline inference, requiring complete inputs before generating outputs.
tail: We make all our code publicly available: https://github.com/EIT-NLP/Speak-While-Watching.

head_q: How does sharing rewards among agents impact their performance in task completion?
tail_q: What percentage of witness-group runs maintain low unsafe completion rates while achieving high legitimate completion?
head: arXiv:2610.09002v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When a team of agents shares a reward for completed tasks, reporting and stopping unsafe work reduces the team's reward.
tail: Only 9 of 48 witness-group runs achieve below 1% unsafe completion while retaining at least 90% legitimate completion.

head_q: How can representing networks as graphs aid in anomaly detection through link prediction?
tail_q: In what ways does CyberGFM improve upon previous methods for unsupervised link prediction in network anomaly detection?
head: Representing networks as a graph and training a link prediction model using benign connections is an effective method of anomaly-based intrusion detection.
tail: We found that CyberGFM outperforms all prior works in unsupervised link prediction for network anomaly detection, using the same number of parameters, and with equal or better efficiency than the previous best approaches.

head_q: What challenges are associated with series elastic actuators in terms of torque and command frequency?
tail_q: How does the Pi-SEA improve performance compared to traditional series elastic actuators?
head: arXiv:2609.30873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A series elastic actuator has a single torque port and pays for it twice: the geared motor must swing its own reflected inertia through the spring, so the amplitude it delivers collapses as $\omega^{-2}$ in the command frequency $\omega$ once it saturates, while commands below the transmission's breakaway friction never arrive at all.
tail: Against SEAs, the Pi-SEA widens the tracked band at small amplitudes and lowers the residual the joint imposes on its environment, each by an order of magnitude.

head_q: What difficulties are involved in detecting deepfakes in video content?
tail_q: How does the proposed approach for video deepfake detection ensure cross-dataset generalization and interpretability?
head: arXiv:2610.03380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deepfake detection in videos remains challenging, as manipulated content may appear visually consistent at the frame level while exhibiting subtle temporal inconsistencies.
tail: The approach also demonstrated a good cross-dataset generalization, providing a robust and interpretable solution for video deepfake detection.

head_q: What are the methods for enhancing spatial resolution in hyperspectral imaging through the fusion of hyperspectral and multispectral images?
tail_q: How does a specific modeling approach improve interpretability and account for non-ideal effects in hyperspectral super-resolution?
head: This work revisits the hyperspectral super-resolution (HSR) problem, i.e., fusing a pair of spatially co-registered hyperspectral (HSI) and multispectral (MSI) images to recover a super-resolution image (SRI) that enhances the spatial resolution of the HSI.
tail: This modeling choice retains interpretability, subsumes CPD, Tucker, and LL1 as special cases, and robustly accounts for non-ideal effects such as EV, offering a balanced tradeoff between expressiveness and interpretability for HSR.

head_q: What role do force field-based molecular dynamics simulations play in understanding biomolecular systems?
tail_q: How can automated frameworks enhance the efficiency and standardization of molecular modeling in drug design?
head: Force field-based molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are indispensable for probing the structure, dynamics, and functions of biomolecular systems, including proteins and protein-ligand complexes.
tail: This automated framework paves the way toward standardized, scalable, and time-efficient molecular modeling pipelines for future biomolecular and drug design applications.

head_q: What social processes are measured when studying climate action resistance through social media archives?
tail_q: How do operational definitions and observation boundaries affect claims about climate backlash?
head: arXiv:2610.07634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Social media archives are often used to study resistance to climate action, but words, response counters and observed participants do not measure the same social process.
tail: These results show how operational definitions, platform-specific response fields and observation boundaries shape what can be claimed about climate backlash.

head_q: What challenges do large language models face in knowledge-intensive tasks due to inaccuracies and outdated information?
tail_q: What improvements in accuracy and efficiency does EA-GraphRAG provide in question-answering benchmarks?
head: Large language models (LLMs) often struggle with knowledge-intensive tasks due to hallucinations and outdated parametric knowledge.
tail: Extensive experiments on a comprehensive benchmark, consisting of two single-hop and two multi-hop QA benchmarks, demonstrate that our EA-GraphRAG significantly improves accuracy, reduces latency, and achieves state-of-the-art performance in handling mixed scenarios involving both simple and complex queries.

head_q: What is the structure of a new database model based on labeled, directed trees?
tail_q: How do analytic queries differ in formulation between the proposed database model and traditional relational models?
head: arXiv:2609.03538v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a novel database model whose basic structure is a labeled, directed tree with node identities.
tail: This is in sharp contrast to the relational model, where analytic queries are defined outside the relational algebra, in the form of SQL Group-by queries.

head_q: What is the significance of Reinforcement Fine-Tuning in aligning preferences in flow-based models?
tail_q: How does ConsistentRFT compare to other methods in terms of performance on out-of-domain metrics?
head: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) on flow-based models is crucial for preference alignment.
tail: Furthermore, ConsistentRFT outperforms other RFT methods on out-of-domain metrics, showing an improvement of 5.1\% (v.s. the baseline's decrease of -0.4\%) over FLUX1.dev.

head_q: How do analyst decisions impact empirical causal claims in research?
tail_q: What are the computational characteristics of exact permutation calibration under randomization?
head: arXiv:2605.01579v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Empirical causal claims depend on many analyst decisions, from selecting covariates to choosing estimators.
tail: We further provide exact permutation calibration under randomization and characterize computation, showing tractable cases under additive structure and NP-hardness in general.

head_q: How can AI assist adults in creating workplace artifacts while maintaining the independence of their reasoning?
tail_q: What engineering properties are supported by the evidence of recorded releases?
head: arXiv:2610.02699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI can help adults produce plausible workplace artefacts while leaving their independent reasoning difficult to inspect.
tail: The evidence supports the tested engineering properties of the recorded release.

head_q: In what ways do performative predictions affect the outcomes they are intended to forecast?
tail_q: What insights can be gained from a case study on job training assignments for unemployed individuals in Germany?
head: Performative predictions influence the very outcomes they aim to forecast.
tail: We illustrate our bounds in a case study on prediction-informed assignments of unemployed German residents to job trainings, drawing upon administrative labor market records from 1975 to 2017 in Germany.

head_q: What challenges exist in medical image segmentation regarding paradigms and data dimensionality?
tail_q: How does UniPro enhance propagation reliability through bidirectional and 3D supervision?
head: arXiv:2610.06938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medical image segmentation remains fragmented along two axes: segmentation paradigms and data dimensionality.
tail: To improve propagation reliability, UniPro further incorporates bidirectional and 3D supervision to regularize slice-wise propagation beyond per-slice losses.

head_q: What are the challenges in energy management due to rising energy costs and sustainability goals?
tail_q: How does automated feature extraction impact operating costs in UK property datasets?
head: arXiv:2609.35013v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The rising cost and demand for energy, together with environmental sustainability goals, create major challenges for energy management.
tail: On a real-world UK property dataset, this approach reduces operating costs by 22.9%-56.5% compared with the same DFL models without automated FE.

head_q: What limitations do Vision-Language Models face in 3D spatial reasoning?
tail_q: How does active exploration in three-dimensional environments enhance spatial reasoning in multimodal agents?
head: arXiv:2601.13029v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While Vision-Language Models (VLMs) excel at 2D visual understanding, they remain constrained by 2D-centric paradigm that severely limits genuine 3D spatial reasoning.
tail: These results show that active exploration in 3D space provides an effective and general paradigm for improving spatial reasoning in multimodal agents.

head_q: What is the stochastic linear bandits model with parameter noise, and how does it function?
tail_q: How does the minimax regret in the classic additive noise model compare to other models?
head: We study the stochastic linear bandits with parameter noise model, in which the reward of action $a$ is $a^\top θ$ where $θ$ is sampled i.i.d.
tail: This is in contrast to the minimax regret attainable for such sets in the classic additive noise model, where the regret is of order $d \sqrt{T}$.

head_q: What computational challenges arise from analyzing needle electromyography signals for neuromuscular disease detection?
tail_q: What strategies can optimize downsampling configurations for near real-time analysis of nEMG signals?
head: Automated analysis of needle electromyography (nEMG) signals is emerging as a tool to support the detection of neuromuscular diseases (NMDs), yet the signals' high and heterogeneous sampling rates pose substantial computational challenges for feature-based machine-learning models, particularly for near real-time analysis.
tail: The results provide practical guidance for selecting downsampling configurations that enable near real-time nEMG analysis and highlight a generalisable workflow that can be used to balance data reduction with model performance in other high-frequency time-series applications as well.

head_q: What are the key challenges in developing models that adapt to distribution shifts in domain generalization?
tail_q: How does a biased imputation model affect prediction error in statistical estimators?
head: Learning models that can handle distribution shifts is a key challenge in domain generalization.
tail: The results show that despite relying on a biased imputation model, the estimator is efficient and achieves lower prediction error, provided the bias is within a reasonable range.

head_q: What is a framework for generating document-centric backgrounds with multi-page editing capabilities?
tail_q: How can a training-free framework ensure coherence and thematic alignment in document generation?
head: We present a framework for document-centric background generation with multi-page editing and thematic continuity.
tail: Our training-free framework produces visually coherent, text-preserving, and thematically aligned documents, bridging generative modeling with natural design workflows.

head_q: What are the benefits of using learnable Koopman operator parameterizations in deep learning forecasting?
tail_q: How effective and stable are learnable Koopman operators in deep forecasting applications?
head: This paper proposes a unified family of learnable Koopman operator parameterizations that integrate linear dynamical systems theory with modern deep learning forecasting architectures.
tail: Our results demonstrate that learnable Koopman operators are effective, stable, and theoretically principled components for deep forecasting.

head_q: How can general-purpose models reduce the need for labeled data in Human Activity Recognition tasks?
tail_q: What impact does deterministic semantic rendering have on recognition performance across datasets?
head: arXiv:2609.36154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: General-purpose models promise sensor-based decisions without training a task-specific classifier, which could reduce the dependence of Human Activity Recognition (HAR) on labeled data.
tail: Instead, they reduce recognition on all three datasets, while augmenting the same numerical evidence with a deterministic semantic rendering partially recovers performance, although the experiment does not isolate semantics from the accompanying serialization and redundancy changes.

head_q: How do manipulation behaviors and skills influence the planning of embodied agents in diverse tasks?
tail_q: What is the relationship between perception updates and library updates in skill-based models?
head: arXiv:2609.36691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Manipulation behaviors vary widely across objects and scenes, but they share a small set of reusable skills, and planning with these skills helps embodied agents generalize to new tasks.
tail: Their errors depend on how perception and library updates are coupled: joint models merge distinct transformations into one skill, while models that update the library from text descriptions duplicate recurring ones.

head_q: How does AI-ECG technology address the detection of multiple pathologies and future risk prediction?
tail_q: What evidence supports the effectiveness of the AnyECG model for concurrent disease detection and risk assessment?
head: Background: Artificial intelligence enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) has demonstrated the ability to detect diverse pathologies, but most existing models focus on single disease identification, neglecting comorbidities and future risk prediction.
tail: Conclusion: The AnyECG foundation model provides substantial evidence that AI-ECG can serve as a systemic tool for concurrent disease detection and long-term risk prediction.

head_q: How can leaders be identified in robotic swarms during adversarial missions?
tail_q: What real-world experiments validate the sim-to-real transfer in robotics?
head: Identifying the leader within a robotic swarm is crucial, especially in adversarial contexts where leader concealment is necessary for mission success.
tail: Real-world experiments with physical robots further validate the approach, confirming successful sim-to-real transfer and robustness to dynamic changes, such as unexpected agent disconnections.

head_q: What are the challenges of unsupervised image registration for complex anatomical structures?
tail_q: How does an implicit visual reasoning approach improve unsupervised medical image registration?
head: Unsupervised deformable image registration requires aligning complex anatomical structures without reference labels, making interpretability and reliability critical.
tail: By embedding an implicit visual reasoning paradigm, we present an interpretable, reliable, and clinically viable unsupervised medical image registration.

head_q: What role does Monte Carlo Tree Search play in robotic decision-making?
tail_q: How does intermediate feedback enhance search refinement in decision-making processes?
head: Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) has emerged as a powerful tool for decision-making in robotics, enabling efficient exploration of large search spaces.
tail: Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of intermediate feedback in search refinement, particularly in pruning incorrect decision paths early.

head_q: What techniques are needed for precise force regulation when manipulating everyday objects?
tail_q: How does RETAF utilize wrist images and tactile feedback for force regulation?
head: arXiv:2602.10013v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Successfully manipulating many everyday objects, such as potato chips, requires precise force regulation.
tail: RETAF regulates force at high frequency using wrist images and tactile feedback, while a base policy predicts end-effector pose and gripper open/close action.

head_q: In what ways does agent memory contribute to the development of LLM-based applications?
tail_q: How does the Hindsight model improve accuracy on long-horizon conversational memory benchmarks?
head: Agent memory has been touted as a dimension of growth for LLM-based applications, enabling agents that can accumulate experience, adapt across sessions, and move beyond single-shot question answering.
tail: On key long-horizon conversational memory benchmarks like LongMemEval and LoCoMo, Hindsight with an open-source 20B model lifts overall accuracy from 39% to 83.6% over a full-context baseline with the same backbone and outperforms full context GPT-4o.

head_q: What advancements have LLMs made towards achieving Artificial General Intelligence?
tail_q: What evidence supports TRPA's performance and stability in reasoning tasks?
head: Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have rapidly evolved, approaching Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) while benefiting from large-scale reinforcement learning to enhance Human Alignment (HA) and Reasoning.
tail: Experimental results demonstrate that TRPA not only achieves competitive performance on reasoning tasks but also exhibits robust stability.

head_q: How does socio-demographic prompting affect the outputs of Large Language Models?
tail_q: What are the limitations of personalization in LLM performance across different behaviors?
head: Socio-demographic prompting (SDP) - prompting Large Language Models (LLMs) using demographic proxies to generate culturally aligned outputs - often shows LLM responses as stereotypical and biased.
tail: However, performance with both behavior types diminishes and becomes nearly equal at the individual level, indicating limits to personalization.

head_q: Why is accurate information retrieval important in the financial sector?
tail_q: How can LLM behavior in finance be quantitatively assessed?
head: Accurate information retrieval (IR) is critical in the financial domain, where investors must identify relevant information from large collections of documents.
tail: This design enables to provide a quantitative basis for understanding retrieval-centric LLM behavior in finance.

head_q: What challenges do Counter-UAV systems face with thermal infrared detection in evolving datasets?
tail_q: What factors contribute to the collapse of large-target detection in per-stratum analysis?
head: arXiv:2610.08315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Counter-UAV systems based on thermal infrared detection must stay accurate as operational datasets evolve, yet sequential fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting of prior tasks, a problem that remains insufficiently characterized in this domain.
tail: Per-stratum analysis shows large-target detection collapsing to near zero within the first epoch, despite an inter-stage cosine similarity of 0.987 over the gradient-updated weights, pointing to scale-conditioned gradient imbalance, rather than weight drift, as a candidate mechanism.

head_q: How have understanding and generative models in computational pathology diverged?
tail_q: What evaluation hierarchy can be established for assessing pathology models?
head: In computational pathology, understanding and generation have evolved along disparate paths: advanced understanding models already exhibit diagnostic-level competence, whereas generative models largely simulate pixels.
tail: For a comprehensive assessment, we establish a four-tier evaluation hierarchy tailored to pathology.

head_q: What are the advantages of using convolutional neural networks in two-view correspondence learning compared to multilayer perceptrons?
tail_q: Where can I find the source code for recent research on neural networks?
head: Recent research has focused on using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) as the backbones in two-view correspondence learning, demonstrating significant superiority over methods based on multilayer perceptrons.
tail: Source code is available at http://www.linshuyuan.com.

head_q: What role do safety monitors play in managing language-model agents interacting with external environments?
tail_q: How does the framework for safety monitoring in language models operate without alarm safety labels?
head: arXiv:2610.02925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety monitors help safeguard language-model agents interacting with external tools and environments, but conservative monitoring can generate many false alarms, consuming extensive review resources and weakening trust in alerts.
tail: The framework requires no alarm safety labels for fitting and leaves the underlying monitor unchanged.

head_q: How have recent developments in large language models advanced the capabilities of conversational AI?
tail_q: Is there a repository of research papers focused on conversational agents available online?
head: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have propelled conversational AI from traditional dialogue systems into sophisticated agents capable of autonomous actions, contextual awareness, and multi-turn interactions with users.
tail: We maintain a curated repository of papers at: https://github.com/emrecanacikgoz/awesome-conversational-agents.

head_q: What is the trend in applying machine learning techniques in dermatology?
tail_q: How can the gap between current AI models and clinical needs in dermatology be quantified?
head: arXiv:2610.03193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The application of machine learning to dermatology has grown substantially in recent years, moving beyond proof-of-concept studies toward potential applications.
tail: By quantifying the gap between current state-of-the-art models and the requirements of clinical deployment, we aim to contribute to the development of reliable, accessible, and clinically applicable AI systems for dermatology.

head_q: In what ways is artificial intelligence changing the research process for discovering new solutions?
tail_q: What improvements in algorithm performance have been achieved by ADRS compared to human designs?
head: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is starting to transform the research process as we know it by automating the discovery of new solutions.
tail: In multiple instances, ADRS discovers algorithms that outperform state-of-the-art human designs (e.g., achieving up to 5.0x runtime improvements or 50% cost reductions).

head_q: How is full-body motion tracking utilized in augmented and virtual reality applications?
tail_q: What evidence supports the superior performance of KineST in motion tracking accuracy and consistency?
head: Full-body motion tracking plays an essential role in AR/VR applications, bridging physical and virtual interactions.
tail: Extensive experiments demonstrate that KineST has superior performance in both accuracy and temporal consistency within a lightweight framework.

head_q: What is the importance of spatio-temporal understanding for autonomous robotic systems?
tail_q: How does the 4DSG framework enable visual language models to interpret spatial and temporal dynamics?
head: Autonomous robotic systems require spatio-temporal understanding of dynamic environments to ensure reliable navigation and interaction.
tail: The resulting 4DSG forms a queryable, unified world model through which VLMs can directly interpret spatial scene structure and temporal dynamics.

head_q: What is Direct Preference Optimization and how does it improve language model alignment?
tail_q: How does GraphDPO achieve linear complexity in its construction?
head: arXiv:2605.08037v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) aligns language models using pairwise preference comparisons, offering a simple and effective alternative to Reinforcement Learning (RL) from human feedback.
tail: Under this layered construction, GraphDPO maintains linear per-prompt complexity via efficient log-sum-exp aggregation.

head_q: What recent architectural advancements have been made in linear sequence modeling?
tail_q: Where can I find the code for the Linear-MoE model?
head: Linear Sequence Modeling (LSM) like linear attention, state space models and linear RNNs, and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) have recently emerged as significant architectural improvements.
tail: Code: https://github.com/OpenSparseLLMs/Linear-MoE.

head_q: How has the combination of pre-trained models and multiple instance learning enhanced diagnostic accuracy in computational pathology?
tail_q: What performance metrics does WSD-MIL achieve on the CAMELYON16 and TCGA-BRCA datasets?
head: In recent years, the integration of pre-trained foundational models with multiple instance learning (MIL) has improved diagnostic accuracy in computational pathology.
tail: Experimental results demonstrate that WSD-MIL achieves state-of-the-art performance on the CAMELYON16 and TCGA-BRCA datasets while reducing 62% of the computational memory.

head_q: How can biological and clinical markers be integrated to characterize the varied presentations of Parkinson's disease?
tail_q: What does interpretability analysis reveal about the decision-making process in clinical assessments of Parkinson's disease?
head: Characterising the heterogeneous presentation of Parkinson's disease (PD) requires integrating biological and clinical markers within a unified predictive framework.
tail: Interpretability analysis shows a clinically coherent decision process, with approximately 60 percent of predictive weight assigned to clinical assessments, consistent with Movement Disorder Society diagnostic principles.

head_q: What is JMMMU-Pro and how does it contribute to multimodal understanding in image analysis?
tail_q: How does JMMMU-Pro enhance the evaluation of Japanese language models and what guidelines does Vibe Benchmark Construction provide?
head: This paper introduces JMMMU-Pro, an image-based Japanese Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding Benchmark, and Vibe Benchmark Construction, a scalable construction method.
tail: We believe that JMMMU-Pro provides a more rigorous evaluation tool for assessing the Japanese capabilities of LMMs and that our Vibe Benchmark Construction also offers an efficient guideline for future development of image-based VQA benchmarks.

head_q: What are the advantages of streaming GPU solvers like FlashSinkhorn for entropic optimal transport?
tail_q: What is the significance of solving large discrete entropic optimal transport problems with high accuracy in a short time?
head: arXiv:2610.02395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Streaming GPU solvers for entropic optimal transport (EOT), such as FlashSinkhorn, avoid storing the dense kernel but still evaluate all $n\times m$ point pairs in every Sinkhorn iteration.
tail: To our knowledge, it is the largest discrete EOT problem solved to this accuracy within hours.

head_q: Why is accurate segmentation of macular edema critical for diagnosing vision-threatening conditions?
tail_q: How does the computational efficiency of a segmentation model impact its precision and performance?
head: Accurate segmentation of macular edema, a hallmark pathological feature in vision-threatening conditions such as age-related macular degeneration and diabetic macular edema, is essential for clinical diagnosis and management.
tail: The model maintains a low computational cost of 0.37 TFLOPs, striking an effective balance between segmentation precision and inference efficiency.

head_q: What role does state estimation play in robotics and extended reality (XR) applications?
tail_q: How does VkVIO facilitate low-latency and cost-effective visual inertial odometry in robotics?
head: arXiv:2609.30459v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Perception in robotics and XR fundamentally relies on good state estimation.
tail: VkVIO enables possibilities for low-latency, low-power, and low-cost VIO in robotics and XR.

head_q: How do generative molecular design benchmarks influence drug-like property predictions in pharmaceutical research?
tail_q: What insights can machine learning provide for nanotechnology through the discovery of new structural motifs?
head: arXiv:2606.30170v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generative molecular design is shaped by simple proxy benchmarks for drug-like properties and models pretrained on large pharmaceutical datasets.
tail: Our results surpass state-of-the-art physical properties and reveal previously unknown structural motifs, offering new insights for the nanotechnology community and demonstrating that ML can drive genuine scientific discovery.

head_q: What advancements are being made with Bird's-Eye-View transformers for 3D object detection using multiple cameras?
tail_q: How does our method improve performance metrics on the nuScenes dataset for 3D object detection?
head: In current research, Bird's-Eye-View (BEV)-based transformers are increasingly utilized for multi-camera 3D object detection.
tail: Evaluating our method on the nuScenes dataset shows consistent and significant improvements in NDS and mAP over the baseline, even with sparser BEV grids and therefore fewer initial anchors.

head_q: What is Dynamic Rank Reinforcement Learning (DR-RL) and how does it optimize multi-head self-attention in language models?
tail_q: How does this research improve the efficiency and theoretical foundations of rank reduction techniques in deep learning?
head: We propose Dynamic Rank Reinforcement Learning (DR-RL), a novel framework that adaptively optimizes the low-rank factorization of Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) in Large Language Models (LLMs) through the integration of reinforcement learning and online matrix perturbation theory.
tail: This work bridges the gap between adaptive efficiency and theoretical rigor in MHSA, offering a principled, mathematically grounded alternative to heuristic rank reduction techniques in resource-constrained deep learning.

head_q: What challenges do large language models face regarding latency and power consumption across different hardware platforms?
tail_q: Where can the ELANA profiling tool for language models be accessed?
head: The latency and power consumption of large language models (LLMs) are major constraints when serving them across a wide spectrum of hardware platforms, from mobile edge devices to cloud GPU clusters.
tail: We release the ELANA profiling tool at: https://github.com/enyac-group/Elana.

head_q: What are the roles of forward forecasting and data assimilation in physical simulations?
tail_q: How does our method compare to existing models on the Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation in terms of inference speed?
head: arXiv:2602.02832v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Forward forecasting and data assimilation are the two important aspects in physical simulation: one propagates the state forward, the other recovers unknown states from sparse observations.
tail: Experiments are performed on the Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equation and a transient flow, and we compare our method against a range of baselines on the forward problem, including diffusion models and operator-learning models, and obtain a 110x inference speedup over strong diffusion baselines.

head_q: What are the recent developments in neural representations that enhance style transfer in 3D environments?
tail_q: How does stylization improve the structure and visual coherence of images?
head: Recent advancements in neural representations, such as Neural Radiance Fields and 3D Gaussian Splatting, have increased interest in applying style transfer to 3D scenes.
tail: This results in a more structured, visually coherent, and artistically enriched stylization.

head_q: What challenges do climbing robots face in achieving agility similar to that of animals in vertical terrains?
tail_q: What design strategies can improve the jump-climbing abilities of robots to match animal agility?
head: arXiv:2609.31014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Animals such as squirrels and even bears have adapted to rapidly climb up trees and other complex vertical terrain, but achieving comparable agility has been a challenge for climbing robots.
tail: Our work proposes design insights for the jump-climbing maneuver and serves as an important step toward creating climbing robots with agility on par with that of animals.

head_q: What advantages do continuous diffusion language models offer for language processing tasks?
tail_q: How does the introduction of discrete reveals to DoubleCat enhance its performance in language modeling?
head: arXiv:2610.13834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) promise to bring the benefits of continuous flow modelling to language, including accelerated sampling and controllable generation.
tail: To address it directly, we introduce discrete reveals to $\mathrm{DoubleCat}$, yielding $\mathrm{SemiCat}$, which achieves discrete diffusion-level performance on TinyGSM, reaching $49.94\%$ with standard training hyperparameters and a tuned sampler.

head_q: Why are generative reward models significant for optimizing large language models?
tail_q: How is MetaCritic optimized during the training of generative reward models to align with human evaluative standards?
head: arXiv:2610.05370v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Generative reward models (GRMs) are important for LLM optimization.
tail: During GRM training, MetaCritic is further optimized to generalize human-grounded evaluative criteria to outcome-only data.

head_q: What role do large language models play in evaluating the outputs of other models?
tail_q: How does reduced reasoning effort impact the accuracy and leniency of evaluations in language models?
head: arXiv:2610.05094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Researchers increasingly use Large Language Models as judges (LLM-as-a-judge) to evaluate model outputs.
tail: Counterintuitively, lower reasoning effort affects neither accuracy nor leniency.

head_q: What applications utilize agentic language model systems to address context limitations?
tail_q: How does the accuracy and information conveyance of a 7B Qwen-2.5 compressor compare to its 1.5B version?
head: Agentic language model (LM) systems power modern applications like "Deep Research" and "Claude Code," and leverage multi-LM architectures to overcome context limitations.
tail: A 7B Qwen-2.5 compressor, for instance, is $1.6\times$ more accurate, $4.6\times$ more concise, and conveys $5.5\times$ more bits of mutual information per token than its 1.5B sibling.

head_q: What is KFS-Bench and how does it facilitate evaluation in long video question answering?
tail_q: How does an adaptively balanced sampling method improve key frame selection and question answering performance?
head: We propose KFS-Bench, the first benchmark for key frame sampling in long video question answering (QA), featuring multi-scene annotations to enable direct and robust evaluation of sampling strategies.
tail: Our adaptively balanced sampling approach achieves superior performance in both key frame sampling and QA performance.

head_q: What compositional elements are common in real-world scenes, both natural and human-made?
tail_q: How does SCION improve upon Gaussian compression methods for scene editing and animation?
head: arXiv:2610.02322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world scenes are compositional: bricks, blades of grass, pebbles, and tree leaves recur across human-built and natural environments.
tail: SCION achieves rate-distortion favorable to existing Gaussian compression methods, and it enables instance-level scene editing and animation without retraining.

head_q: What is the significance of developing faster algorithms for Mixed-Integer Linear Programming in practical applications?
tail_q: How does DeepBound perform on complex instances of Mixed-Integer Linear Programming?
head: Designing faster algorithms for solving Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) problems is highly desired across numerous practical domains, as a vast array of complex real-world challenges can be effectively modeled as MILP formulations.
tail: Moreover, DeepBound demonstrates strong generalization capability on large and complex instances.

head_q: What shortcomings do large language models exhibit when functioning as autonomous agents with tool-use capabilities?
tail_q: What evaluation methods are necessary for effective deployment of agentic models in interactive environments?
head: We investigate how large language models (LLMs) fail when operating as autonomous agents with tool-use capabilities.
tail: These patterns highlight the need for agentic evaluation methods that emphasize interactive grounding, recovery behavior, and environment-aware adaptation, suggesting that reliable enterprise deployment requires not just stronger models but deliberate training and design choices that reinforce verification, constraint discovery, and adherence to source-of-truth data.

head_q: What are the applications of self-supervised models in EEG signal processing?
tail_q: Do performance improvements in spectral cue tasks apply to motor imagery and mental health assessments?
head: arXiv:2610.07484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-supervised EEG models often reconstruct masked waveforms or predict discrete codes.
tail: The gains do not extend to every task with spectral cues, including motor imagery, depression screening, and vigilance regression.

head_q: How does text style transfer function as a supervised task in natural language processing?
tail_q: What are the performance comparisons of RT-SFT against few-shot learning methods in style transfer?
head: arXiv:2602.15013v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Text style transfer (TST) is naturally a supervised task - rewrite a sentence in a target style while preserving its meaning - yet the parallel corpora that supervision requires exist for only a handful of style domains.
tail: We show that across four style domains, RT-SFT outperforms state-of-the-art methods, such as few-shot in-context learning, by considerable margins.

head_q: What challenges do phasor measurement units face in wide-area measurement systems?
tail_q: How effective is the proposed method in handling high missing data rates in measurements?
head: In wide-area measurement systems (WAMS), phasor measurement unit (PMU) measurement is prone to data missingness due to hardware failures, communication delays, and cyber-attacks.
tail: Numerical results demonstrate the superior offline and online performance of the proposed method under high missing rates and incomplete observability.

head_q: What is the role of the Attentive VLM Agent in enhancing gameplay experiences in StarCraft II?
tail_q: Where can I find the implementation of the VLM-Play-StarCraft2 project?
head: We introduce Attentive VLM Agent (AVA), a multimodal StarCraft II agent that aligns artificial agent perception with the human gameplay experience.
tail: Our implementation is available at https://github.com/camel-ai/VLM-Play-StarCraft2.

head_q: How does multimodal object detection with RGB and IR images improve perception in adverse weather?
tail_q: What datasets validate the performance of SLGNet in object detection tasks?
head: Multimodal object detection leveraging RGB and Infrared (IR) images is pivotal for robust perception in all-weather scenarios.
tail: Extensive experiments on the LLVIP, FLIR, KAIST, and DroneVehicle datasets demonstrate that SLGNet establishes new state-of-the-art performance.

head_q: What are the benefits of modular end-to-end systems in autonomous driving?
tail_q: How does the proposed ME2E framework affect driving performance and system efficiency?
head: Modular end-to-end (ME2E) autonomous driving paradigms combine modular interpretability with global optimization capability and have demonstrated strong performance.
tail: Experiments across multiple ME2E autonomous driving stacks show that the proposed framework preserves baseline-level driving performance while significantly reducing inference latency and energy consumption, achieving substantial overall system-level improvements.

head_q: What is the SWE-Game benchmark and what tasks does it include?
tail_q: How do visual scores correlate with human ratings in gameplay assessments?
head: arXiv:2609.33678v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce SWE-Game, a benchmark of 247 tasks grounded in 41 executable reference Godot games spanning 13 gameplay categories in 2D and 3D.
tail: Rubric-based visual scores reach a Spearman correlation of 0.829 with human ratings of 200 gameplay clips.

head_q: What is distribution matching distillation and how is it applied in text-to-image generation?
tail_q: What advantages does AF-Loss provide in model training without adding complexity?
head: arXiv:2609.38156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distribution matching distillation (DMD) provides a general framework for few-step diffusion generation, but its modern text-to-image instantiations have been developed primarily around latent diffusion.
tail: AF-Loss adds no learnable parameters or inference-time computation.

head_q: How do search filters impact booking conversions in platforms like Airbnb?
tail_q: What improvements does SIFT bring to booking and amenity engagement metrics?
head: arXiv:2610.07810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Search filters help guests navigate vast catalogs in two-sided marketplaces like Airbnb, and recommending the right filters can meaningfully lift booking conversion.
tail: Offline, SIFT improves booking and amenity-engagement PR-AUC by +51.9% and +62.8% respectively over the production baseline.

head_q: How do looped language models enhance computational efficiency in AI?
tail_q: What insights do studies provide on the effectiveness of recurrent computation in LoopLMs?
head: arXiv:2609.36636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Looped language models (LoopLMs) increase computational depth through parameter sharing, offering a path to scale inference computation without adding parameters.
tail: Overall, our results clarify when recurrent computation helps, where it fails, and offer practical guidelines for designing LoopLMs across variable inference budgets.

head_q: What are the computational challenges of deploying latent diffusion models like Stable Diffusion for image restoration on edge devices?
tail_q: How does NanoSD serve as a diffusion model for real-time visual generation on edge devices?
head: Latent diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion 1.5 offer strong generative priors that are highly valuable for image restoration, yet their full pipelines remain too computationally heavy for deployment on edge devices.
tail: NanoSD establishes a general-purpose diffusion foundation model family suitable for real-time visual generation and restoration on edge devices.

head_q: What are the limitations of traditional LiDAR-inertial odometry methods in terms of environmental feature reliance?
tail_q: How does FMCW-LIO compare to other algorithms in terms of accuracy and robustness in various scenes?
head: arXiv:2609.29374v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Conventional LiDAR-inertial odometry (LIO) or simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) methods heavily rely on geometric features of environments, as LiDARs primarily provide range measurements instead of motion measurements.
tail: Extensive experiments in diverse scenes are performed and FMCW-LIO outperforms other algorithms on both accuracy and robustness.

head_q: What are time series foundation models and how are they trained on diverse datasets?
tail_q: What inconsistencies exist in the reporting of training loss for existing time series foundation models?
head: arXiv:2610.07324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) are trained on large collections of time series datasets that span various morphologies and domains.
tail: Notably, existing TSFMs use both objectives, with neither consistent reporting nor a common convention on how to compute training loss.

head_q: What challenges does AI face in oncology due to the need for large annotated datasets?
tail_q: How do smaller open-source models like Paligemma and CLIP perform in resource-constrained clinical settings?
head: The application of AI in oncology has been limited by its reliance on large, annotated datasets and the need for retraining models for domain-specific diagnostic tasks.
tail: Notably, open-source models like Paligemma and CLIP demonstrated competitive gains despite their smaller size, suggesting feasibility for deployment in computing constrained clinical environments.

head_q: What is the role of federated learning in decentralized machine learning while preserving privacy?
tail_q: How does PSI-guided clustering improve robust performance in personalized federated learning with label skew?
head: Federated learning (FL) supports privacy-preserving, decentralized machine learning (ML) model training by keeping data on client devices.
tail: These results establish PSI-guided clustering as a principled, lightweight mechanism for robust PFL under label skew.

head_q: What is the current use of convolutional neural networks for multi-class segmentation in medical imaging?
tail_q: What are the challenges associated with obtaining accurate labels for 3D data regions of interest?
head: Convolutional neural networks (CNN) for multi-class segmentation of medical images are widely used today.
tail: Obtaining accurate labels for the regions of interest can be an expensive and time-consuming process, particularly for 3D data.

head_q: What novel approach is proposed for annotating brain vasculature using dynamic 4D-CTA scans?
tail_q: Where can the code and model weights for robust vessel segmentation be accessed?
head: In this study, we develop a novel methodology for annotating the brain vasculature using dynamic 4D-CTA head scans.
tail: Our code and model weights are available online: https://github.com/alceballosa/robust-vessel-segmentation

head_q: Why are large-scale 3D motion datasets important for understanding pedestrian interactions in autonomous driving?
tail_q: Where can the dataset and code for Waymo-3DSkelMo be found?
head: Large-scale high-quality 3D motion datasets with multi-person interactions are crucial for data-driven models in autonomous driving to achieve fine-grained pedestrian interaction understanding in dynamic urban environments.
tail: The dataset and code will be available at https://github.com/GuangxunZhu/Waymo-3DSkelMo

head_q: What is Open-Environment Active 3D Mapping and its significance in embodied intelligence development?
tail_q: How are candidate paths generated from anchors through obstacle-aware planning?
head: arXiv:2609.36889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To advance the development of embodied intelligence, Open-Environment Active 3D Mapping has attracted increasing attention, aiming to perform a long-horizon and shortest trajectory exploration for reconstructing unseen scenarios.
tail: These anchors are first converted into executable candidate paths through obstacle-aware planning.

head_q: What factors influence the forecasting of sparse time series in terms of retaining past data and borrowing from others?
tail_q: What issues arise in diagnostic reports regarding the refinement of learned mixtures in partition objectives?
head: arXiv:2511.12749v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Forecasting many sparse series requires two choices: how much of each series' own past to retain, and how much to borrow from other series.
tail: On four panels the diagnostic reports at most $0.6\%$ of room for refinement and realized gains are no larger; on the one panel with room the learned mixture does not collect it, which locates the open problem in the partition objective.
